rules.name: Overview and Course
rules.desc:
The honors program aims to extend and deepen work done in Film and Media Studies classes. The honors thesis topic typically emerges from prior coursework; it should be focused and have clear parameters. Ordinarily, an honors thesis is an exploration of an area the student has already studied.
Admission to the Honor Program
The minimum requirement for admission to the honors program is an overall GPA of 3.5 and at least 3.5 in Film & Media Studies courses. Students must complete at least five Film & Media Studies courses at Stanford by the end of their junior year, and four must be completed by the end of Winter Quarter.
Submission of the Thesis Proposal
Candidates for the honors program must submit a five-page (double-spaced) thesis proposal, including bibliography and illustrations, and one completed paper that demonstrates the student’s ability to conceptualize and write cogently about art historical issues. A complete application is due to the proposed thesis advisor on March 31.
Submission and Approval of the Honors Thesis
Students must submit the final draft of their honors thesis to their faculty advisor, the second faculty reader, the Student Services Specialist, and the Honors Director by the thesis deadline.
More Information
For more information about the Art History and Film & Media Studies Honors Program, students can visit the department website.
rules.notes: During their senior year, students enroll in two to five units of FILMEDIA 297 - Honors Thesis Writing each quarter for a total of 10 units.

grading: All courses must be taken for a letter grade.
policies:
Eligible students may also pursue a Bachelor of Arts in Film & Media Studies with Honors.
Courses may not be offered every year and are subject to change. Students can consult their faculty advisor or the Student Services Specialist if a course is not listed below.
transferPolicy: Students can take a maximum of two courses (ten units) away from Stanford; this includes transfer courses from other universities and Bing Overseas Studies Program. Students must meet with their advisor and the Student Services Specialist before planning an overseas campus program.
reviewNotes: Every course must be letter graded. You take the foundation courses (ARTHIST 1A or 1B, and FILMEDIA 4 and 6 for 5 units each), FILMEDIA 101 and 102 (102 is also Writing in the Major) and two film history courses for at least 4 units each, one studio course, the FILMEDIA 290 capstone, and five subplan electives of at least 4 units, for 61 units. Culture and Criticism allows at most one FILMPROD course among its five, and Screenwriting needs at least one FILMEDIA course among its five. Your advisor approves your subplan electives and checks the library orientation, an Art History elective used in place of ARTHIST 1A or 1B, and courses taken away from Stanford (at most two). Honors adds 10 units of FILMEDIA 297, the 3.5 GPA overall and in the major, and an approved proposal and thesis.
